name: Odyssey-3
description: Odyssey's foundation world model, an autoregressive diffusion transformer that predicts in real time how a text-prompted environment changes as a person or agent acts in it; also used to drive robot, vehicle, drone and game policies.
strengths: Real-time interaction via a distilled few-step variant
Odyssey-3 Pro scores 66.1 on Physics-IQ Verified video-to-video (vendor-reported; claimed highest reported score)
First- and third-person navigation plus agent-introduced events in the preview
weaknesses: Research preview only; no published developer pricing or API
Low base resolution (832x480; 1280x720 only for Pro)

pricing.notes: No product pricing published; developers asked to get in touch. Preview at experience.odyssey.systems (press coverage says free; not stated on Odyssey's page).

notes: Announced 2026-09-15 ('Introducing Odyssey-3', said public release 'in the coming weeks'); research preview made available 2026-10-08 ('Our research preview is available now'), used as releaseDate. maxResolution is the Pro variant (base Odyssey-3 is 832x480, per a benchmark footnote). Physics-IQ and WorldMark figures are Odyssey's own evaluations. openWeights false = no weights mentioned anywhere. Predecessor Odyssey-2 Max (2026-04-21) was private beta for partners only. Odyssey also lists Agora-2 (multi-agent world model, 2026-09-24) with a demo at agora.odyssey.systems — not added as a separate entry. Notable=false only because access is 'research preview', not ga/beta, though the preview appears open to anyone — caller may wish to override.

name: GWM Worlds 2
description: Runway's real-time interactive world model that turns video-and-audio generation into a steerable simulation: users define environment, subjects, style, physical rules and ambience, then steer with free-form text actions and continuous camera motion.
strengths: Continuous 720p video at 24 fps with generated 48 kHz audio, including matched speech and lip movement
No preset session length; Runway says it 'can generate indefinitely'
Free-form text actions addressed to subjects or the scene, bindable to keys
weaknesses: Research preview gated behind a contact form; no pricing or API
Runway notes real-time generation trades fidelity for speed; fast camera rotations degrade detail
Long-term memory is imperfect

pricing.notes: Not published. Access by contact form.

notes: maxSessionSec null because Runway states sessions have 'no preset length' rather than a cap. Image input = a first frame (image references beyond the first frame not supported). Builds on GWM-1 (2025-12-11; GWM Worlds/Avatars/Robotics variants) — GWM Worlds v1 not added separately; its current availability is not stated on Runway's pages. openWeights false = none mentioned.

name: Atlas
description: World Labs' 'omni' world model, trained from scratch on text, images, video and 3D, that generates and reconstructs scenes as video or as point clouds / 3D Gaussian splats with precise camera control.
strengths: Outputs up to 1 minute of video at 1440p
Exports worlds as point clouds or 3D Gaussian splats (same representation as Marble)
Single model covers generation and reconstruction from one to dozens of images
weaknesses: Early access with select partners only
No real-time generation claimed
notes: Also accepts 3D inputs and depth maps (not in the inputs enum). maxSessionSec 60 = maximum video output length, not an interactive session. interactive null: the page describes camera control but not real-time interaction. World Labs says Atlas will power future versions of Marble. World Labs announced on 2026-09-28 that it agreed to be acquired by AMD (expected to close by end of 2026); product plans not stated.

name: Alaya-EVOKE
description: Open-weight, three-step, CFG-free interactive video world model from Alaya Lab with camera control and mid-rollout prompt switching, aimed at endless long-horizon rollouts.
strengths: Open weights (Apache-2.0) with training and inference code
Camera-controlled rollouts with per-chunk prompt switching
Faster than playback in the Director UI on five H200s (1.5 s chunks in 1.34 s)
weaknesses: Low resolution (384x640)
Slower than real time on a single H200 (1.5 s of video every 2.11 s)
Required depth backend is CC-BY-NC-4.0, which restricts commercial use
notes: releaseDate = paper date on Hugging Face (arXiv 2608.13546, 'Published Aug 13'); GitHub news has a Day-0 WBench entry 2026-08-14, Evoke-Turbo (14B, controllability-tuned) 2026-09-11 and interactive UI 2026-09-12. Repo is Apache-2.0 but the required ViGeo depth model (and optional Depth-Anything-3) is CC-BY-NC-4.0, so commercialUse true applies to the repo only. 'actions' = camera pose tracks / movement and look controls. Documented coherence is 30 s rollouts; 'hour-scale' rollouts are described but no measured result (a third-party report's 65-minute figure was not found on primary pages). Predecessor AlayaWorld (2026-07-08, HF AlayaLab/AlayaWorld) not added separately. Alaya Lab's affiliation: paper lists USTC, Shanghai Innovation Institute and Alaya Lab; no lab website found.

name: ABot-World-0
description: Open-weight 5B action-conditioned interactive video world model from Alibaba's AMAP CV Lab that streams open-ended worlds on a single consumer GPU.
strengths: 720p at up to 16 FPS on a single RTX 5090 (~19 GiB peak VRAM)
1.2 s action-to-first-frame latency
Apache-2.0 open weights plus browser studio and HF Space demo
Experimental 24-hour uninterrupted rollout demo published
weaknesses: 16 FPS ceiling relies on optimized low-bit configurations

pricing.notes: Free open weights; ABot World Studio at abot-world.amap.com.

notes: Developer is AMAP (Alibaba's mapping/location unit) CV Lab — mapped to company 'alibaba' (companies.json name is 'Alibaba (Qwen)'; caller may prefer a separate id). releaseDate = HF news log 'We release the causal student model' 2026-07-09; paper arXiv 2607.19191 submitted 2026-07-21. maxSessionSec null: the model claims open-ended generation; the 24-hour run is described as an experimental demo, not a limit.

name: LingBot-World 2.0 (Infinity)
description: Open-weight real-time interactive world model from Robbyant, Ant Group's embodied-AI unit, with an unbounded interaction horizon, rich in-world actions, and Pilot/Director agents.
strengths: Real-time model claimed sufficient to drive 720p streams at 60 fps
Unbounded interaction horizon; Robbyant's release claims hour-long continuous generation
Rich actions (attacking, archery, spell-casting, shooting) plus text-driven events
Playable online via Reactor (international) and LingGuang (China)
weaknesses: Non-commercial licence (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)
Example inference runs at 480P on 8 GPUs; real-time hardware not specified

pricing.notes: Free open weights (non-commercial). Hosted play on Reactor; Reactor pricing not checked.

notes: Initial release 2026-07-09 (tech report, inference code, 14B causal-fast); GitHub says remaining variants (14B causal-pretrain, 14B bidirectional, 1.3B causal) followed 2026-09-10, though its TODO list was still unchecked. 720p/60fps is the developer's claim for the real-time model; the published inference example is 480x832. Hour-long figure comes from Robbyant's own Business Wire press release, not the repo (repo says 'unbounded interaction horizon'; only a 1-minute rollout demo is listed). Robbyant mapped to 'ant-group'.

name: Oasis 3
description: Decart's real-time, action-conditioned world model for physical AI that streams three synchronized camera views of one continuous environment, sold by the second through Decart's API.
strengths: Available by public API from launch ('the first world model accessible by API, live from day one')
Sub-200 ms end-to-end latency at 22 FPS
Closed-loop interaction of 'unbounded length'
weaknesses: Low per-view resolution (512x768)
Billed as a 'Preview' model

pricing.notes: $0.02 per second of generation (a 60 s session = $1.20); enterprise pricing on request.

notes: Resolution conflict: launch post says 512x768x3 (three synchronized views); the pricing page says the $0.02/s rate is 'at 720p'. access set to 'beta' because the API model id and pricing page label it 'Oasis 3 Preview'. Positioned for robotics/AV simulation rather than consumer play. Decart's Lucy 2.5 (real-time video editing) excluded as not a world model.

name: Cosmos 3
description: NVIDIA's open omnimodal world foundation model family for physical AI that reasons about and generates text, images, video, ambient sound and actions, usable as a world/video model, VLM, or backbone for robot policies.
strengths: Open weights under a commercial-use licence (OpenMDW 1.1)
Action-conditioned forward-dynamics generation as well as inverse-dynamics and policy modes
Two sizes released: Nano (16B) for workstation GPUs, Super (64B) for large-scale synthetic data
NVIDIA reports first place among open models on Physics-IQ and RoboArena
weaknesses: Not a real-time interactive generator; produces clips of 5-400 frames
Edge variant for real-time inference not yet released

pricing.notes: Free open weights; also via build.nvidia.com, NVIDIA NIM, and cloud partners (Baseten, CoreWeave, Azure, Nebius, Deep Infra, Classmethod) — partner pricing not checked.

notes: Announced at GTC Taipei; press release and model cards date it 2026-05-31 (some coverage says June 1). Output resolution/fps follow the input request; 720p is the maximum listed input resolution and the examples use 1280x720 at 24 fps, so fps left null. Clip length 5-400 frames (default 189); maxSessionSec left null as no duration is stated (400 frames ≈ 16.7 s at 24 fps, my arithmetic). Super is listed as 64B in NVIDIA's HF blog and 65B on the HF page. Audio input supported (max 0.5 s) — not in the inputs enum. A third variant, Cosmos 3 Edge, is 'coming soon'. OpenMDW SPDX id not confirmed, so spdx null.

name: Echo-2
description: SpAItial's 3D world generation model that turns a text prompt or image into a persistent, explorable 3D Gaussian-splat scene (with semantic segmentation) rather than a video.
strengths: Persistent 3D scene, rendered in real time in the browser on any device
Exports SPZ, PLY, SOG and collision meshes
Public API with a free tier (800 credits/month)
Vendor reports it beats Marble 1.1 on WorldScore scene-quality metrics
weaknesses: Static scenes: dynamics and physics-based behaviour are listed as future work

pricing.notes: API: 1 credit = $0.01; Echo-2 world = 160 credits (~$1.60), Echo HQ = 800 credits (~$8). Plans: Free 800 credits/mo, Standard 7,500, Pro 15,000 (plan prices not listed on the docs page).

notes: interactive true = user navigates the generated static scene in real time; generation itself is asynchronous. Also accepts 360° panoramas and floor plans. apiIds value is the example string from the docs ('model': 'Echo 2'); exact ids should be confirmed via GET /v1/models. Docs also mention Echo HQ (May 2026 checkpoint) and an 'Echo-3' whose API access requires Enterprise — no Echo-3 announcement found, so not added. WorldScore comparison is vendor-run.

name: HY-World 2.0
description: Tencent HY's open multimodal 3D world model that generates, reconstructs and simulates editable 3D worlds (meshes, 3D Gaussian splats, point clouds) from text, images or video, exportable to game engines.
strengths: Editable 3D outputs (mesh, 3DGS, point cloud) rather than transient video
Open weights and inference code; free online trial
Generated worlds support first/third-person navigation with physics-based collision; render in real time on consumer GPUs
weaknesses: Licence excludes the EU, UK and South Korea and needs Tencent's permission above 1M MAU
Components were released in stages (full world-generation code only from 2026-05-18)

pricing.notes: Free open weights; free trial at 3d.hunyuan.tencent.com/sceneTo3D.

notes: Staged release: 2026-04-16 tech report + WorldMirror 2.0 weights; 2026-05-11 HY-Pano 2.0; 2026-05-18 world-generation code + WorldStereo 2.0 weights. GitHub README announces an 'HY World 2.1' update (July 2026) linked to the product page, with no model card or weights — not added as a separate entry. commercialUse true with conditions: licence grant is royalty-free within the Territory (worldwide excl. EU/UK/South Korea) and >1M MAU requires a licence from Tencent. interactive true = navigation of generated scene; generation is not real-time.

name: Happy Oyster
description: Real-time open-ended world model from Alibaba's ATH (Alibaba Token Hub) unit with joint audio-video generation, offering a Directing mode to steer a live scene and a Wandering mode to explore a world in first person.
strengths: Directing mode: steer a live scene for up to 3 minutes at 480p or 720p via text, voice or images
Wandering mode: first-person exploration with WASD and camera controls
Continuous joint audio-video generation
Pay-per-second API on fal
weaknesses: Wandering mode limited to 1 minute at 480p
Official site access still by application; closed weights

pricing.notes: fal: billed per second of generated world, no minimums; per-second rate not shown on fal's pages.

notes: Exact day (2026-04-16) is from press coverage (Bloomberg/SCMP); fal's official partner page says only 'unveiled in April 2026'. access 'beta': limited early access by application on happyoyster.cn, but fal (official API partner) lists it as 'available now'. maxSessionSec 180 = Directing mode; Wandering is 60 s at 480p. Voice input also supported. A third fal path /explore exists but its API id is unconfirmed. A 'Happy Oyster 2 Preview' for the 2026 Yunqi conference is reported by a third-party listing only — not confirmed on any Alibaba page, not added.

name: Lyra 2.0
description: NVIDIA research framework that turns a single image plus a camera path into a large, persistent, walkable 3D Gaussian scene by generating camera-controlled video and lifting it to 3D.
strengths: Outputs 3D Gaussian scenes (.ply), exportable as splats or meshes
Per-frame 3D geometry used to retrieve past frames and limit spatial forgetting/drift
Isaac Sim integration demonstrated for robot simulation
weaknesses: Weights licensed for internal scientific research only — no production or commercial use
Single-image input at 480x832

license.name: NVIDIA Internal Scientific Research and Development Model License

pricing.notes: Free weights for research use; self-hosted.

notes: Model card release date 04/14/2026 (GitHub). 14B parameters, built on Wan-14B per secondary coverage. Code is Apache-2.0 on GitHub (nv-tlabs/lyra) but weights are research-only. Camera-pose input not in the inputs enum. interactive true = navigation of the generated static scene. Borderline inclusion: a research release, but weights are publicly downloadable.

name: Waypoint-1.5
description: Overworld's open-weight real-time world model that runs locally on consumer GPUs or streams in the browser, generating a playable first-person world that reacts to keyboard and mouse input.
strengths: Up to 720p at 60 FPS on high-end consumer GPUs; a 360p tier for wider gaming-PC support
Apache-2.0 open weights
Runs locally via the Biome installer or in-browser via Overworld.stream
weaknesses: 512-frame context length
No text prompting listed on the model card (image/video conditioning only)

pricing.notes: Free open weights; whether Overworld.stream is free is not stated.

notes: Parameter count inconsistent on the model card (1.2B in text vs 2B in HF metadata). Successor Waypoint 2 ('latest frontier world model', text or image input) is invite-only beta with no date or specs published — not added. 60 FPS quoted for the 720p tier as 'up to'.

name: Marble 1.1 / 1.1 Plus
description: World Labs' generally available multimodal world model that turns text, images, multi-view images, panoramas or video into navigable, editable 3D worlds (Gaussian splats and meshes), with a Plus variant for larger worlds.
strengths: Exports Gaussian splats (SPZ/PLY), collider and high-quality GLB meshes, and panoramas
Broad input set: text, single image, multi-image with azimuths, 360° panoramas, video
In-app editing, world expansion, composition and Chisel 3D layout sculpting
Public World API alongside a consumer app with a free tier
weaknesses: Generation takes about 5 minutes per world
Static scenes, not a real-time simulation

pricing.notes: API: $1 per 1,250 credits; marble-1.1 world = 1,500-1,600 credits (~$1.20-1.28); marble-1.1-plus 1,500-3,100 credits depending on world size; HQ mesh export 3,500 credits. App plans: Free (up to 4 worlds), Standard $20/mo (20,000 credits), Pro $35/mo, Max (up to 75 worlds), Enterprise custom; app and API credits are separate.

notes: Date conflict: Marble release notes list 1.1 and 1.1 Plus under 2026-04-02; World Labs' X post saying 'rolling out ... today' is timestamped 2026-04-07 (used). Marble itself went GA 2025-11-12; World API launched 2026-01-21. Marble 1.0 / 1.0 Draft remain selectable (marble-1.0, marble-1.0-draft) but not added separately. interactive true = navigation/editing of generated static scene. Max plan price not on the docs page (a stale-indexed pricing page shows $95/mo; unverified). World Labs agreed to be acquired by AMD (announced 2026-09-28). RTFM (real-time frame model research preview, 2025-10-16) not added.

name: Matrix-Game 3.0
description: Skywork AI's open-source real-time streaming interactive world model with camera-aware long-horizon memory, fine-tuned from Wan2.2-TI2V-5B.
strengths: 720p at 40 FPS real-time generation with the 5B model (developer claim)
Stable memory consistency over minute-long sequences
Open weights (Apache-2.0) and MIT-licensed code
weaknesses: Larger 28B MoE (2x14B) version described but no download link
Multi-GPU inference setup in examples; hardware for real-time not specified

pricing.notes: Free open weights; self-hosted. No hosted product found.

notes: Weights card says Apache-2.0; GitHub repo (code) says MIT. Release date 2026-03-27 from GitHub news; HF card says only '2026-03'. Input device for actions not named on the card ('--interactive' mode with user actions).

name: Genie 3 (Project Genie)
description: Google DeepMind's general-purpose real-time world model, available to consumers through the Project Genie prototype (with Nano Banana Pro and Gemini) to sketch, explore and remix playable worlds from text and images.
strengths: Real-time navigable photorealistic worlds at 720p, 20-24 fps
Environments stay largely consistent for several minutes, with visual memory of about a minute
Street View-grounded worlds of real U.S. places (since 2026-05-19)
Available to Google AI Ultra subscribers globally (18+)
weaknesses: Project Genie generations capped at 60 seconds
Requires the $200 Google AI Ultra plan; not available on Ultra for Business; no API
Google notes higher control latency and imperfect prompt/physics adherence; promptable world events not in the prototype

pricing.notes: Included with Google AI Ultra ($200 tier), 18+.

notes: Genie 3 was announced 2025-08-05 as a limited research preview for select academics/creators; releaseDate is the first public launch via Project Genie (2026-01-29, U.S. Ultra subscribers), expanded to Ultra subscribers globally on 2026-05-19. Google calls Project Genie 'an experimental research prototype', hence access 'research-preview' even though any eligible paying subscriber can use it. fps: DeepMind model page says 20-24 fps, the Genie 3 blog says 24. maxSessionSec 60 = Project Genie cap; the model itself supports 'a few minutes' of continuous interaction. No Genie 4 found.

name: HY-World 1.5 (WorldPlay)
description: Tencent HY's open-source real-time interactive streaming video world model with long-term geometric consistency, responding to keyboard and mouse input; the video-stream counterpart to HY-World 2.0's 3D output.
strengths: Real-time streaming at 24 FPS with keyboard/mouse control
Reconstituted context memory for long-term geometric consistency
Open training code, inference code and weights; online demo
weaknesses: Only a 480p model released
Licence excludes the EU, UK and South Korea and needs Tencent's permission above 1M MAU

pricing.notes: Free open weights; online demo at 3d.hunyuan.tencent.com/sceneTo3D.

notes: Included alongside HY-World 2.0 because it is a separate, still-offered line (real-time video stream vs 3D asset generation). HF card: 'Now we only provide the 480p model' (secondary coverage claims 720p — not on primary pages). No max length stated ('infinite world extension'; default 125 frames). Built on HunyuanVideo 1.5. commercialUse true with the same territory/MAU conditions as HY-World 2.0.
